features.name: Crisis Safety System (§9 Deterministic Gate)
features.mechanism: Three-layer fail-closed crisis detection: (1) deterministic keyword floor (suicidal/self-harm lexicons across English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu scripts + slang + euphemism/pre-suicide prep co-occurrence gates), (2) additive on-device MiniLM semantic classifier (catches euphemistic disclosures the keyword floor misses), (3) output gate (checkResponse Rules 1–6) ensuring every AI reply surfaces crisis resources, blocks method instructions, validates no cognitive distortions, affirms no euphemistic death-peace phrases, and blocks sycophantic/mania-affirming replies. Crisis text never persists or leaves device.
features.currentEvidence: Cited in code: scanForCrisis keyword lists with paired benign-control tests; crisisClassifier weights trained on MiniLM embeddings; checkResponse Rules 1–6 with MANIC_VALIDATION. EVIDENCE.md notes: 'Cross-validated recall ≈ 89% (from ≈ 61% keyword-only), not 100% — will miss cases; English classifier is the only ML layer and is additive-only.'
keyCitations: Stanley & Brown 2012 (Safety Plan) ✓ in safetyPlan.ts
Linehan 2015 DBT crisis survival skills ✓ in skillsLibrary.ts
Østergaard 2023 (sycophancy in LLM mental health) ✓ in safety.ts MANIC_VALIDATION
MiniLM sentence embeddings (Reimers & Gurevych) — classifier weights in crisisClassifier.weights.json
features.clinicalProtocol: Stanley-Brown Safety Plan (6 steps) with 48h + 14d follow-up loop (safetyPlanFollowUp.ts); Crisis lines region-aware (IN/US/GB/CA/AU + international fallback). Deterministic keyword scan is the universal floor; classifier is additive soft upgrade (fail-closed).
strengthGaps: Classifier is English-only; non-English disclosures rely solely on keyword floor
~8% earnest false-alarm rate on soft classifier (acceptable only for soft nudge, not hard hijack)
No 100% recall guarantee — 'it will miss cases' (EVIDENCE.md)
Euphemism/pre-suicide prep gate requires co-occurrence; single-cue veiled disclosures can slip
No external clinician alerting — purely on-device surface

features.name: Social Rhythm Tracking (IPSRT-Based)
features.mechanism: Daily anchor logging (wake, breakfast, lunch, dinner, wind-down, bed, custom). Computes per-anchor mean time and variability (minutes) over rolling window. Regularity bands: regular / variable / irregular / insufficient (<3 days). Dashboard shows anchor timing ± variability. Fused with sleep data in circadianFeedback (combined score 0–100 + guidance). Research basis: Monk Social Rhythm Metric (1990/1991) as used in IPSRT (Frank 2005). IPSRT 2026 RCT: η²=0.37 rhythm stability, η²=0.49 social functioning. CRM app: 3.39× episode recurrence reduction.

The evidence for rhythm regularity is strongest for bipolar disorder and rests on a small number of trials; the bands here are a self-reflection aid, not a clinical measure or a diagnosis.' PLAN_OF_ACTION.md: 'IPSRT 2026 RCT: η²=0.37 improvement in social rhythm stability, η²=0.49 in social functioning. CRM app: 3.39× episode recurrence reduction.'

features.name: Grounding & Breathing Library
features.mechanism: GroundingLibraryScreen: expandable cards for 5-4-3-2-1 senses, box breathing (4-4-4-4), paced breathing (4-6), body scan, TIPP temperature, self-soothe 5 senses. BreathingTimer: configurable breath pacer (in/hold/out/hold). Tools → In the moment → Grounding & breathing. WindDown uses 4-in/6-out.
features.currentEvidence: skillsLibrary.ts: 54321 (grounding, consistent with MBCT Segal et al. 2002), box-breathing (Thayer & Lane 2009 vagal tone), TIPP (Linehan 2015). Grounding techniques: core component of trauma-focused CBT and DBT (Najavits 2002; Linehan 1993) — cited in protocols.ts Grounding & Anchor basis.
